questions.question: What could happen if the fifth wheel plate is not greased properly?
questions.explanation: A fifth wheel plate that is not greased creates friction between the tractor and trailer. This friction causes steering problems.

questions.question: If a parked trailer has no spring brakes, how should you keep it from moving?
questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks to prevent a parked trailer without spring brakes from moving. Air brakes only work while there is air pressure in the tanks. Wheel chocks provide reliable protection.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: one service line and one emergency line.

questions.question: How can you avoid making sudden lane changes?

options.text: Use your horn to make other drivers move.
Only drive slower than the speed limit.
Look ahead at the road while driving.
Pull off the road when traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead at the road while driving.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous when driving a combination vehicle. Look down the road for obstacles ahead so you can change lanes smoothly and safely when needed.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
Only the rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open except the rear ones.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open except the rear ones.
questions.explanation: Keep all shut-off valves open except the rear ones. This ensures air reaches the brakes on all trailers and prevents air from escaping from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving a combination vehicle, what type of stops should you make?
questions.explanation: Brake well in advance and look far ahead. These habits prevent your trailer from jackknifing and help you stay safe.

questions.question: What happens if a load is placed on one side of a trailer?

options.text: The trailer may lean and could roll over.
The trailer gets extra support during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may lean and could roll over.
questions.explanation: A load placed on one side of a trailer causes it to lean. This increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent a trailer from rolling over?

options.text: Speed up when nearing a corner.
Drive faster than the speed limit on ramps.

questions.explanation: Drive slowly around corners to reduce rollover risk. Keep the cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: What happens when trailer wheels lock up?

options.text: The cab swings but the trailer stays straight.

questions.explanation: When trailer wheels lock up, the trailer swings out and can strike other vehicles. This is especially dangerous with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface to see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and look for an ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Check under older trailers for wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes to see if they have ABS.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Triple combinations are most likely to roll over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: It is located on the front of a trailer.
It is located on the dashboard.
It stops air from leaving the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must always be closed to keep air in the brake system.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a jackknife?
questions.explanation: During a jackknife, release the brakes to help your tires grip the road. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: During a sudden turn, which trailer is most likely to roll over?
questions.explanation: Turn slowly and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: When driving a truck with ABS, how should you brake?

options.text: Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake using less pressure than normal.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a truck with ABS as you would in a truck without ABS.

questions.question: When glad hands are color-coded, which color marks the emergency line?
questions.explanation: When trailer air lines are color-coded, blue marks service lines and red marks emergency lines.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A device that keeps air in the truck's brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the truck's brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects the truck's air brake system by keeping air in if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling, what should you do under the trailer?

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Look into the back of the fifth wheel to check that the jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes too quickly with a trailer?

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that causes a rollover.
Other drivers get confused about your direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that causes a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle can cause a "crack-the-whip" effect that results in a rollover.

questions.question: When driving a combination truck, how should your following distance compare to a single vehicle?

options.text: It should be shorter in bad weather.
It should be about the same.

questions.explanation: Keep a longer following distance in a combination truck than in a single vehicle. Combination trucks need more distance to stop.
